import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
from sklearn.impute import KNNImputer
from sklearn.datasets import load_iris
from sklearn.metrics import mean_squared_error

def knn_imputation_demo():
    # Load Iris dataset
    iris = load_iris()
    X = iris.data.copy()
    
    # Introduce missing values (20%)
    np.random.seed(42)
    mask = np.random.random(X.shape) < 0.2
    X_missing = X.copy()
    X_missing[mask] = np.nan
    
    print(f"Missing values introduced: {np.isnan(X_missing).sum()}")
    
    # KNN imputation with different k values
    for k in [3, 5, 7]:
        imputer = KNNImputer(n_neighbors=k)
        X_imputed = imputer.fit_transform(X_missing)
        
        # Calculate MSE only on originally missing values
        mse = mean_squared_error(X[mask], X_imputed[mask])
        print(f"KNN (k={k}): MSE = {mse:.4f}")
    
    # Show sample imputation
    imputer = KNNImputer(n_neighbors=5)
    X_imputed = imputer.fit_transform(X_missing)
    
    print("\nSample comparison (first 5 rows, first 2 columns):")
    print("Original:")
    print(X[:5, :2])
    print("With missing:")
    print(X_missing[:5, :2])
    print("Imputed:")
    print(np.round(X_imputed[:5, :2], 2))

knn_imputation_demo()
